concepts.name: Big-O notation
concepts.gloss: Asymptotic upper bound on growth of a function, ignoring constant factors.

concepts.name: Polynomials
concepts.gloss: Finite sums of coefficients times powers of a variable, added and multiplied coefficientwise.

concepts.name: Complex numbers
concepts.gloss: Numbers a+bi with i²=−1, including unit-modulus roots of unity e^{2πi/k}.

concepts.name: Turing machines and tapes
concepts.gloss: A finite-state machine reading and writing symbols on tapes with moving heads.

concepts.name: Fixed finite-tape machine model
concepts.gloss: The computation model: one fixed finite alphabet and a fixed number of one-dimensional tapes, each step touching one cell per tape, so extra tracks or work tapes change time only by a constant factor.

evidence.quote: A machine has one fixed finite alphabet and one fixed finite number of one-dimensional tapes.

concepts.name: The n log n optimality conjecture
concepts.gloss: Schönhage and Strassen's proposal that n log n is the optimal order of growth for multiplying n-bit integers on multitape Turing machines.

evidence.quote: proposed $n\log n$ as the optimal order of growth

concepts.name: Established O(n log n) multiplier (Harvey–van der Hoeven)
concepts.gloss: The known fixed-tape integer multiplier running in O(N log N) time on N-bit inputs, used here only as an ordinary subroutine on short records.

evidence.quote: the fixed-tape integer multiplier of Harvey and van der Hoeven
Calls to the established $O(n\log n)$ multiplier are ordinary subroutine

concepts.name: Arrays in lexicographic tape order with address fields
concepts.gloss: A multidimensional array is stored on a tape in lexicographic order of its address (first coordinate most significant), so address fields are contiguous ranges of positions and an address is implicit in position.

evidence.quote: lexicographic order, with the first coordinate most significant

concepts.name: Elementary stream operations
concepts.gloss: Linear-time tape scans that permute digit values, move a digit, split an array by a digit, apply a pointwise map and merge, or split whole rows cyclically into a fixed number of equal streams.

evidence.quote: takes $O(V)$ steps on a fixed number of one-dimensional tapes

concepts.name: Controlled cyclic shifts and rational scalings
concepts.gloss: In linear time, update a target address field by adding an offset computed from earlier control fields modulo q^b (a cyclic shift of blocks), or multiply it by a fixed rational unit.

evidence.quote: Controlled shifts and fixed rational scalings

concepts.name: Matrix rank, subspaces and orthogonal complements
concepts.gloss: Rank of a matrix, subspaces of a vector space with a bilinear form, and the orthogonal complement of one subspace inside a larger one, whose dimension equals the change in dimension.

evidence.quote: the orthogonal complement of the smaller label inside the larger one
Every rational $m\times m$ matrix $A$ of rank $a$ has a factorization

concepts.name: Discrete Fourier transform
concepts.gloss: The normalized map sending a length-q vector u to (F_q u)_k = (1/q) Σ_j u_j e^{−2πi jk/q}; its inverse-direction version uses the opposite sign, and both are contractions.

evidence.quote: (F_q u)_k=\frac1q\sum_{j=0}^{q-1}u_j e^{-2\pi i jk/q}

concepts.name: Cyclic convolution
concepts.gloss: Multiplication of polynomials (or arrays) modulo x^S − 1, where indices wrap around modulo the length on every axis.

evidence.quote: let $*$ denote cyclic convolution in the displayed axes

concepts.name: Convolution theorem for normalized transforms
concepts.gloss: The transform of a cyclic convolution equals the pointwise product of transforms (with a normalizing factor), so convolution can be computed by transform, pointwise product and inverse transform.

concepts.name: Multidimensional (tensor) transforms
concepts.gloss: A transform on a product of axes of lengths t_1,…,t_D, equal to the tensor product of the one-dimensional transforms applied along each axis in turn.

evidence.quote: F_{\boldsymbol t}^\pm=\bigotimes_{i=1}^D F_{t_i}^\pm

concepts.name: Integer multiplication as digit convolution
concepts.gloss: Writing each input in radix 2^b digits makes the product's digit sequence a convolution of the two coefficient lists; with enough zero padding, cyclic convolution equals ordinary polynomial multiplication, and carrying recovers the integer.

evidence.quote: Splitting the inputs into radix digits reduces multiplication to convolution of short integer coefficients.

concepts.name: Fixed-point disk grid and error propagation
concepts.gloss: Complex values stored as pairs of signed fixed-point integers with p fractional bits in the unit disk; algorithms approximate linear contractions, truncation toward zero adds bounded error, and errors add under composition.

evidence.quote: \mathbb D_p=\{2^{-p}(a+ib):a,b\in\mathbb Z,\ a^2+b^2\leq 2^{2p}\}

concepts.name: Polynomial ring modulo y^r + 1
concepts.gloss: Complex polynomials of degree below r with y^r = −1, so multiplication by a power of y is a signed cyclic shift of the coefficient list (negacyclic wraparound).

evidence.quote: \mathcal R_r=\mathbb C[y]/(y^r+1)

concepts.title: Polynomial ring modulo $y^r+1$

symbols.name: ring variable
symbols.meaning: The polynomial variable, which satisfies y^r = −1 and serves as a root of unity.

symbols.name: coefficient count
symbols.meaning: The number of complex coefficients in a polynomial record, a power of two.

concepts.name: Two-point butterfly and radix-2 FFT order
concepts.gloss: The butterfly H₀(u,v) = ((u+v)/2, (u−v)/2) applied recursively by decimation in frequency, with twiddle multiplications, computes a transform of power-of-two length and leaves outputs in bit-reversed slot order.

evidence.quote: the decimation-in-frequency step pairs $z_k$ with $z_{k+t/2}$

concepts.name: Synthetic polynomial transform
concepts.gloss: A Fourier-type transform of arrays of ring polynomials in which the roots of unity are powers y^{2r/t}, so twiddle multiplications are exact signed shifts of coefficient lists and only butterflies cost arithmetic.

evidence.quote: synthetic polynomial transforms of Nussbaumer and Quandalle and Nussbaumer
For a power of two $t$ dividing $2r$, define $\omega_t=y^{2r/t}$.

concepts.name: Chinese-remainder address map
concepts.gloss: A ring isomorphism from cyclic convolution of length S = s_1⋯s_d (pairwise coprime) to d-dimensional cyclic convolution on prime axes, implemented on tape by triangular prefix-controlled cyclic shifts.

evidence.quote: Agarwal and Cooley used the Chinese remainder theorem to convert one cyclic convolution into multidimensional cyclic convolution

concepts.name: Gaussian resampling with retained permutations
concepts.gloss: Harvey–van der Hoeven's identity expressing a Fourier transform of coprime length s through one of power-of-two length t via Gaussian-weighted maps A and B₀, here keeping the two coordinate permutations inside the formula instead of sorting.

evidence.quote: Gaussian resampling then expresses each source Fourier transform through a power-of-two tensor transform.
P_sF_s=2^{2\alpha^2}B_0P_tF_tA

concepts.name: Bluestein chirp identity
concepts.gloss: Rewrites a Fourier transform (with its frequency permutation) as pointwise multiplication by a quadratic phase, a cyclic convolution with the chirp array, and another pointwise phase multiplication.

evidence.quote: Bluestein's chirp identity converts the middle transform, including its target permutation, into normalized cyclic convolution

concepts.name: Source-permutation cancellation
concepts.gloss: The coordinate permutation retained by resampling cancels across the two forward transforms, their pointwise product and the opposite-sign transform, leaving (u*v)/S² so no sort is executed.

evidence.quote: Finally, the source permutation retained during resampling cancels across the two forward source transforms, their pointwise product, and the opposite-sign transform.

concepts.name: Coefficient twist to negacyclic ring
concepts.gloss: Multiplying coefficient k by ζ^k with ζ = e^{πi/r} maps cyclic convolution on the last axis to convolution in the ring of polynomials modulo y^r+1, whose negative wrap exactly cancels the twist.

evidence.quote: A phase twist changes the last cyclic coordinate into a polynomial modulo $y^r+1$; its negative wrap gives precisely the original cyclic wrap after the twist is removed.

concepts.name: Linear exchange network with restored scratch wires
concepts.gloss: A fixed network of linear gates on wires (roles) that swaps two banks of values with prescribed signs and returns every auxiliary scratch wire to its arbitrary initial value, using a copy/gather/scatter/side-injection schedule.

evidence.quote: We construct two fixed linear networks that exchange two banks of values while restoring every auxiliary value.

concepts.name: Frames and the common-frame identity
concepts.gloss: Giving each array on a wire an invertible address-space operator (a frame) at every vertex; because a common frame commutes with a pointwise linear gate, the network's overall effect is the endpoint frames applied to each role, and each edge only changes the frame.

evidence.quote: the common frame commutes with the pointwise gate
D_{\rm out}\,\mathsf S_\Omega\,D_{\rm in}^{-1}

concepts.name: Three-element-subset subspace labels
concepts.gloss: Subspaces of a tensor-cube bilinear space attached to gates, built from indicator vectors of three-element subsets with intersection-size pairings (Frankl–Wilson, Alon), so labels are nested along edges and neighbors are orthogonal.

evidence.quote: Let $\mathcal T$ be the set of three-element subsets of $[h]$.

concepts.name: Rank deficit s < Wm
concepts.gloss: Summing the dimension changes (edge ranks) of all labels gives a total s of smaller calls strictly below W·m, where W is the number of wires and m the dimension, which is the source of the power saving.

evidence.quote: The decisive property is that the total number $s$ of smaller calls satisfies $s<Wm$.

concepts.name: Bit exchange network with shear interface
concepts.gloss: The F₂ network with rational labels whose frames are address shears: its endpoint operator is (H,D)→(H+D,D) on every role, using only XOR gates, with rank sum s_b < W_b m.

evidence.quote: The bit network has $W_{\rm b}$ wires, uses only pointwise XOR gates,

concepts.gloss: The Z[i,1/2] network with binary labels whose frames are phase operators C_U = H^{⊗m} diag(i^{wt(P_U x) mod 4}) H^{⊗m}; each edge is a product of two-point kernels aI+bX_v and the endpoint operator is C^{⊗m} on every role, with s_c < W_c m.

evidence.quote: For each edge of the complex network, write $U,V$ for its tail and

concepts.name: Lower-triangular factorization of matrices
concepts.gloss: Every rational matrix A of rank a factors as E₁ΠE₂ with E₁,E₂ invertible lower triangular and Π a partial permutation with a ones (a reversed-order Bruhat factorization).

evidence.quote: Every rational $m\times m$ matrix $A$ of rank $a$ has a factorization

concepts.name: Rational matrix shear as field interchanges
concepts.gloss: The map (H,D)→(H+AD,D) over Z/q^b for a rank-a rational matrix A is performed by triangular controlled shifts and exactly a interchanges of b-digit fields.

evidence.quote: The cost of a rational matrix shear

concepts.name: Power-saving recurrence
concepts.gloss: Calling s smaller operations of parameter f/m on streams of volume V/W gives normalized cost F_k ≤ (s/W)F_{k−1}+O(1); since s/W < m^τ this solves to O(e^τ), a strict power saving.

evidence.quote: F_0=O(1),\qquad F_k\le(s/W)F_{k-1}+O(1).

concepts.name: Power-width address interchange with rows
concepts.gloss: Interchanges two chunks of m^k digits using the bit network: split rows among the W roles, apply a matrix shear on each edge via recursive smaller interchanges, merge, then compose three shears into a swap.

evidence.quote: Power-width interchange with rows

concepts.name: Fast interchange of address chunks
concepts.gloss: Exchanges two disjoint address chunks of u bits in an array (any prefix, gap and suffix) in O(V u^τ) tape steps for a fixed τ < 1, by padding rows and splitting the width in base m; the final effect is an exact permutation although intermediate steps form XOR combinations.

evidence.quote: Arbitrary-width interchange
The first procedure interchanges two disjoint contiguous address fields of $u$ bits

concepts.title: Fast interchange of $u$-bit address chunks in $O(Vu^\tau)$

symbols.name: chunk width
symbols.meaning: The number of bits in each of the two address chunks being interchanged.

symbols.name: stored bit volume
symbols.meaning: The number of data bits stored in the array.

symbols.name: interchange exponent
symbols.meaning: A fixed constant with 0 < τ < 1 (here 1 − 2^{-50}) in the exponent of the cost.

concepts.name: Packed selected-bit addition with deterministic repair
concepts.gloss: Performs y←y⊕x on the same bit position of f chunks at once using eight cyclic shifts of whole chunk ranges (a three-chunk rotation trick that restores a scratch chunk), then corrects the small explicitly identified set of addresses where guard values fail.

evidence.quote: Packed selected-bit addition on one rectangle

concepts.name: Simultaneous butterfly layer
concepts.gloss: Applies the two-point butterfly H₀ at one bit position in each of D address chunks at once in O(V d^{λ'}) time, by recursing on the complex phase network with packed basis changes, exact Gaussian-dyadic arithmetic and one final truncation.

evidence.quote: Simultaneous normalized butterfly layer

concepts.title: Simultaneous butterfly layer $H_0^{\otimes D}$

symbols.name: axis count
symbols.meaning: The number of address chunks, one selected bit in each, on which the butterfly acts simultaneously.

concepts.name: Synthetic transform layout and stored frequency order
concepts.gloss: Places selected bits of all participating axes at a common offset in consecutive chunks so each radix-two round is one simultaneous layer, and keeps the bit-reversed frequency order through the pointwise product to the opposite transform.

evidence.quote: Transform layout and cost

concepts.name: Signed packing (Kronecker substitution)
concepts.gloss: Multiplies two ring polynomials by evaluating them at B₀=2^{4p} as signed integers, multiplying with the O(N log N) integer multiplier, extracting centered coefficients and wrapping negacyclically.

evidence.quote: The reduction is a signed form of Kronecker substitution

concepts.name: Convolution over the polynomial ring from the retained layout
concepts.gloss: Computes normalized convolution of arrays of ring polynomials by two forward synthetic transforms, pointwise ring products by signed packing, and the opposite transform consuming the same stored order.

evidence.quote: Convolution from the retained transform layout

concepts.name: Complex cyclic convolution by coefficient twist
concepts.gloss: Normalized cyclic convolution f*g/T of complex arrays on power-of-two axes, obtained by twisting the last axis into the polynomial ring and using the ring convolution.

evidence.quote: The power-of-two complex convolution used in the chirp identity is obtained from the synthetic convolution by a coefficient twist.

concepts.name: Source transform procedure
concepts.gloss: Computes the transform of coprime length by applying the Gaussian map A line by line, the chirp transform through complex convolution, the map B₀, and an exact power-of-two scale, with the retained permutation R.

evidence.quote: For a source disk-grid tensor of norm at most $.5$, write

concepts.name: Choice of prime source lengths
concepts.gloss: Chooses distinct odd primes s_i just below the powers of two t_i (with t_i/s_i separated from 1) via a prime-interval lower bound, found by deterministic search, so S is a constant fraction of the padded box T.

evidence.quote: The distinct prime lengths $s_i$ must be close to the powers of two

concepts.name: Parameter choice and cost balance
concepts.gloss: Fixes p = Θ(log n), d = ⌊b^ε⌋ axes, chunk size K, ring dimension r = 2^{Θ(p/d)} and the tiny exponents so that every row of the cost table has normalized power of p at most 1 − 2κ, giving total O(n (log n)^{1−κ}).

evidence.quote: lists costs after division by $V$
Thus $\min_i g_i=2^{-181}=2\kappa$.

concepts.name: Rounding and carry propagation to the exact product
concepts.gloss: Shows the recovered coefficient error is below 1/2, rounds to the integer convolution coefficients, and propagates radix-2^b carries to output exactly 2n product bits.

evidence.quote: Propagate radix-$2^b$ carries in increasing coefficient order.

concepts.name: The multiplication algorithm
concepts.gloss: Splits both inputs into digits, applies the coefficient-address map, computes the source transform of each, multiplies pointwise, applies the opposite-sign transform with scalings, rounds and propagates carries.

evidence.quote: The source-transform procedures now supply the three transforms needed for the radix-digit convolution.

concepts.name: Integer multiplication in O(n (lg n)^(1−κ)) time
concepts.gloss: There is one deterministic fixed-alphabet, fixed-tape Turing machine multiplying n-bit integers exactly in O(n (lg n)^{1−κ}) time with κ = 2^{−182}, disproving the n log n optimality conjecture in this model.

evidence.quote: There is one deterministic Turing machine $A$, with a fixed finite alphabet and a fixed finite number of one-dimensional tapes
T_A(n)=O\!\left(n(\lg n)^{1-\kappa}\right)

concepts.title: Integer multiplication in $O(n(\lg n)^{1-\kappa})$ time

symbols.name: operand length
symbols.meaning: The number of bits in each of the two integers being multiplied.

symbols.name: saving exponent
symbols.meaning: The fixed constant 2^{-182} by which the logarithmic factor is reduced.
